title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook centralizes Applied ML evaluation processes used during model onboarding and production lifecycle: eval harness integration, prompt-set and benchmark design, quantization profiling, quality guardrails, and regression triage. It describes roles, repeatable checklists, expected metrics and thresholds, and runbook steps for triage and mitigation.

Scope: Applies to every model variant we consider for serving on Redwood (hosted, dedicated, private). Includes open and vendor models and all supported quantization experiments.

Owners and contacts

- Document owner: Applied ML (Aisha Patel)
- Primary owners: Applied ML team (model-onboarding), Runtime team (quantization kernels), Observability (dashboards and alerts)
- Pager/contact for regressions: eng-oncall@redwood.ai, applied-ml-triage Slack channel (#applied-ml-triage)

High-level workflow

1) Model request/selection: Product or Platform requests model adoption. Create model entry in model registry and open an onboarding ticket.
2) Eval harness integration: Add model to eval-harness suite, implement model adapter and scoring hooks, register CI jobs.
3) Prompt-set design & benchmark run: Curate prompt sets, label expected outputs, run benchmark suites (functional + robustness + safety).
4) Quantization profiling: Run quantization profiles (FP16, INT8, 4-bit families) and record perf/quality tradeoffs.
5) Quality guardrails & thresholds: Define pass/fail thresholds for key metrics and establish canary rollout criteria.
6) Regression triage: On detected regressions run triage playbook, decide mitigation (rollback, fallback model, prompt patch, or accept degradation).

Model Onboarding Checklist (numbered)

1. Create model registry entry: model_name, architecture, pretrained_source, model_size, base_tokenizer, owner, compliance notes.
2. Implement model adapter in eval-harness: ensure same API semantics as other models; include deterministic seeds and sampling configs.
3. Baseline benchmark: run full benchmark suite (prompt-set + safety + perf) and capture artifacts. Attach artifacts to onboarding ticket.
4. Quantization smoke tests: run basic quantization profiles and check inference correctness on 100 control prompts.
5. Cost/latency estimate: record P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, and per-token cost estimate for hosted and dedicated.
6. Review & approval: Applied ML + Runtime + Observability sign-off. If any safety flags appear, Security and Trust must review.

Prompt-set and Benchmark Guidelines

- Prompt-set composition: include 200-2,000 examples depending on vertical. Cover: typical happy-path, edge-cases, adversarial cases, and post-edit checks.
- Templates: include explicit instruction, input, expected behavior, and optional canonical answers. Use the prompt-set item template in Appendix.
- Labeling: labels must include intent, category, difficulty, and expected_score (0-1). Try to include multi-turn contexts where applicable.
- Metrics to capture per-run: helpfulness, correctness, factuality, toxicity, hallucination rate, token utilization, latency P50/P95, cost-per-response.
- CI cadence: Run lightweight smoke benchmarks for every PR; nightly full-suites; weekly cross-model benchmark runs on staging.

Benchmark metric thresholds (example table described)

- Quality thresholds (suggested defaults): helpfulness >= 0.80, correctness >= 0.85 (vertical dependent), toxicity < 1% flagged sentences, hallucination rate < 2% on factual QA sets.
- Performance thresholds: P95 latency <= 200ms for dedicated small models; P95 <= 500ms for large models on dedicated; throughput >= expected tokens/sec target for planned capacity.
- Regression alert thresholds: relative drop in helpfulness > 5 percentage points OR relative latency regression > 20% triggers automated regression-ticket.

Quantization Profiles and Profiling Procedure

- Profile families supported: FP16 (baseline), INT8 (calibrated), 4-bit (AWQ, GPTQ variants). Each profile must be recorded as a named profile (e.g., profile: fp16, int8-calib, awq-4bit).
- Profiling steps:
  1. Run calibration dataset (1k-5k samples) for int8 where applicable.
  2. Run quantized inference across representative prompt-set and record quality metrics + perf counters.
  3. Generate quant-report with: accuracy_delta, per-metric diffs, P50/P95 latency, memory reduction, and failure cases.

- CLI example (replace with real job):
  - python tools/quant_profile.py --model model-name --profile int8-calib --calib-data data/calib-1k.json --out reports/model-int8-report.json

- Recommended acceptance criteria for shipping a quantized variant: accuracy_delta (helpfulness) <= 3 percentage points AND no new safety flags introduced. If not met, escalate to Runtime + Applied ML for kernel or prompt mitigation.

Quality Guardrails

- Automated guardrails: safety filters, toxicity classifiers, and format validators run in eval-harness. Failing items produce diagnostics with offending tokens and prompt context.
- Canary criteria: When promoting a new model/quant profile to canary, require: (a) full benchmark pass, (b) canary traffic limited to 5-10% for 24-72 hours, (c) no critical safety flags, and (d) error budget impact < 0.5%.

Regression Triage Playbook (runbook)

Trigger: Regression alert from eval-harness, alerting pipeline, or customer report.

1) Triage intake (first 30 minutes):
   - Owner: oncall + Applied ML primary
   - Create regression ticket and attach failing eval artifacts (diffs, failing prompts, traces).
2) Reproduce & scope (30-90 minutes):
   - Re-run failing prompts on the model commit that passed last good run and on current candidate. Capture RNG seeds and deterministic configs.
   - Determine scope: prompt sets affected, model variant, quant profile, or infra/latency issues.
3) Severity classification:
   - S0 (critical): safety violation or data leak - immediate rollback and sec review.
   - S1 (high): large quality drop (helpfulness drop > 10 pts) - pause rollout and investigate.
   - S2 (medium): moderate drop (5-10 pts) - mitigation by prompt patches or rollback planned.
   - S3 (low): <5 pts or perf tiny regressions - queued for next sprint.
4) Mitigation actions (examples):
   - Immediate rollback to previous model or quant profile (Owned by Release Engineering).
   - Apply prompt steering patch or response filter (Applied ML).
   - Throttle/cut canary traffic and debug kernel-level perf regressions (Runtime).
5) Postmortem and preventive actions (within 7 days):
   - Owner writes short postmortem in confluence/regression-triage, tags involved teams, and includes: cause, timeline, mitigation, and preventive action items (tests, guardrails, CI changes).

Tools, dashboards, and CI hooks

- Eval-harness repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/eval-harness (adapter patterns and CI job names under ci/eval-*/).
- Dashboards: apml-evals-overview (Grafana), quantization-reports (internal dashboard), regressions-alerts (PagerDuty + Slack).
- CI jobs: nightly-evals, pr-smoke-eval, quant-profile-ci. Ensure any new model adds entries to ci/evals.yml.

Appendix: Prompt-set item template (text fields)

- id: (string)
- prompt: (string - full prompt input)
- context: (optional multi-turn history)
- expected_behavior: (string short description)
- canonical_answers: (list of acceptable outputs)
- labels: (list: intent, category, difficulty)

Appendix: Example eval command

- python -m eval_harness.run --model model-name --prompt-set data/prompt-sets/vertical-x.json --metrics helpfulness,correctness,toxicity --output reports/model-vertical-x-run.json

Notes

- Keep this playbook up-to-date with any changes to eval-harness interfaces and Runtime quant kernels. Major changes must be versioned and referenced in related_pages.
